doc.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998

chapter: Singing in England and moving to North America
title: Moving to Canada and Albany, and the jazz band there
summary: She went to Canada in the 1950s with her first husband, did CBC television, returned, then settled in Albany singing in a band for twelve and a half years before joining Bob.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What circumstances brought you to the United States?

First of all I came to live in Canada in the ‘50s. I suppose in a way you could say that I was importing husbands but I’m not really. I came over with my first husband, who was an actor, and we went to live in Canada, and I was working for CBC, I was very active. I was doing a weekly television show, and not singing, I was acting. I was performing and acting as a showgirl and one thing or the other. Then I went back to England, after doing quite a lot of work, I played a small part in a Frank Sinatra movie, and I did a lot of things, living in Florida, and then I went back to England, and couldn’t seem to settle there. And I married an Englishman who’d been a resident in medicine in Albany, New York and we came back over here. And he was a trombone player, played with a jazz band, and we had a very good jazz band in Albany, New York, for a long time and I sang with that and for twelve and a half years we had a band, very actively playing around, and played a lot of material, and I did a number of festivals. And then we broke up and Bobby and I went off together, and we’ve been together twenty-one years now, which is a long time, although I wish I had it all to do again, I’d have twenty-one more.
